summary.text: The original bug was reproduced and the fix guards against it with no regressions found, but Break My Fix found that days_in_month(year=2200, month=2) still returns 29, so the leap-year logic appears to handle 2100 but not other century years. Look next at the century/400-year rule in billing.calendar.days_in_month and add a test covering years like 2200 and 2000.

property.name: matches_gregorian_calendar
property.claim: The number of days equals the Gregorian calendar's count for every valid month and year, including all century years such as 1900, 2100, 2200, 2300.
property.quote: Return the number of days in `month` (1-12) of `year`.

findings.relation: the same before the fix, but the failing call runs the fix's line(s) 19: the fix touched this path and left it broken

labels.label: intended
labels.reason: The issue reports that 29 Feb 2100 does not exist, so February 2100 must have 28 days. The hardcoded special case is a narrow fix, but this specific input's change is exactly what the issue asks for.

survivors.description: Applies the 28-day override to all years from 2100 onward, not just 2100.
survivors.diff:
--- a/src/billing/calendar.py
+++ b/src/billing/calendar.py
@@ -18,3 +18,3 @@
         raise ValueError(f"month must be 1..12, got {month}")
-    if year == 2100 and month == 2:
+    if year >= 2100 and month == 2:
         return 28
survivors.words: src/billing/calendar.py:19: changing `    if year == 2100 and month == 2:` to `    if year >= 2100 and month == 2:` made no test fail; it behaves differently from the fix on inputs no test checks
